newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on cautious mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on cautious mood.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down on Friday, with most investors more cautious on news of plans to further tighten controls on the financial markets, brokers said.
The index fell 0.474 points or 0.69 percent to 68.545 points on volume of 20.9 million shares worth $8.8 million.
China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji called for measures to provide greater risk control on the financial markets, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday.

The newspaper also reported China's National People's Congress, or parliament, had decided to make securities-related fraud a crime rather than an irregularity in a draft amendment to the Criminal Law.
Brokers said the news helped cool the market's prevailing speculative mood, and this saw investors overcome by caution. They sold, but follow-up buying was thin.

"The recent over-speculative mood on the domestic A share market made investors concerned about measures the government might take to cool things down, and today's news is regarded as a sign," one broker said.
"A correction is needed, with the index rising as it has over the past 10 days," another broker said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 27 down, six flat and 10 up.
Food producer Shanghai Dajiang Group was the biggest loser on speculative selling, tumbling $0.056 or 9.36 percent to $0.542 on thin volume of 1,300 shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai followed on institutional unwinding, slipping $0.014 or 3.68 percent to $0.366 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
